MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a factor of 18? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 5
   C. 6
   D. 7

2. What number is the Roman numeral IV? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 6
   C. 7
   D. 5

3. Round 47 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 60
   B. 0
   C. 50
   D. 40

4. What is the next number in the pattern 10, 15, 20, 25, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 30
   B. 29
   C. 31
   D. 35

5. Which of these shows 583 in words? (1 mark)
   A. six hundred and eighty-three
   B. five hundred and eighty-three
   C. five hundred and thirty-eight
   D. five hundred and ninety-three

6. Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 9,010
   B. 9,099
   C. 8,990
   D. 9,000

7. Work out 6,478 + 2,355. (1 mark)
   A. 8,733
   B. 8,723
   C. 8,833
   D. 8,843

8. What is the rule of the pattern 1,200, 1,500, 1,800, 2,100? (1 mark)
   A. subtract 300
   B. add 600
   C. add 300
   D. add 1,200

9. Which word in a problem tells you to add? (1 mark)
   A. Difference
   B. Fewer
   C. Altogether
   D. Remain

10. Work out 25 × 16. (1 mark)
   A. 390
   B. 400
   C. 175
   D. 410

11. What is 12 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 112
   B. 120
   C. 1,200
   D. 12,000

12. A hen lays 21 eggs in a month. How many eggs do 16 hens lay in a month? (1 mark)
   A. 436 eggs
   B. 316 eggs
   C. 336 eggs
   D. 326 eggs

13. What is 95 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 23 remainder 4
   B. 24 remainder 3
   C. 23 remainder 3
   D. 22 remainder 7

14. 29 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 4 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 8
   C. 9
   D. 7

15. Ali writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 7/4
   B. 1 3/4
   C. 3/8
   D. 11/5

16. In the fraction 3/5, what does the numerator 3 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. The number of wholes
   B. How many of the equal parts are taken
   C. The size of each part in centimetres
   D. How many equal parts the whole has

17. What is 1/10 of 50? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 5
   C. 10
   D. 45

18. Chebet writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 2 5/8
   B. 5/12
   C. 8/3
   D. 9/9

19. In the fraction 4/12, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 16
   C. 4
   D. 12

20. In the number 13.42, the digit 2 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Hundredths
   B. Ones
   C. Tens
   D. Tenths

21. Write 0.37 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 37/100
   B. 3/7
   C. 37/10
   D. 37/1000

22. Why can 2a + 3b not be written as 5ab? (1 mark)
   A. Because 2 + 3 is not 5
   B. Because letters can only be added to numbers
   C. Because ab is not a letter
   D. a and b are different things, so the terms cannot be joined

23. Change 9 m 5 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 95 cm
   B. 14 cm
   C. 9,050 cm
   D. 905 cm

24. What is 6 m 15 cm − 2 m 50 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 55 cm
   B. 3 m 65 cm
   C. 4 m 65 cm
   D. 3 m 75 cm

25. Which unit is used for area? (1 mark)
   A. Centimetres
   B. Square centimetres
   C. Kilograms
   D. Litres

26. A rectangle has an area of 36 square units and 4 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 32
   B. 10
   C. 9
   D. 40

27. A rectangle has an area of 60 square units and 5 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 55
   B. 13
   C. 12
   D. 65

28. A square is covered with 8 rows of 8 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 64 square units
   B. 16 square units
   C. 72 square units
   D. 32 square units

29. Which statement about a cube is true? (1 mark)
   A. It has only 4 faces
   B. Its length, width and height are equal
   C. It has no corners
   D. Its length is double its width

30. Cuboid A is 6 by 2 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 3 by 3 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot be told
   B. Cuboid B
   C. Cuboid A
   D. They are equal

31. A tank has 50 L of water and 18 L is used. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 42 L
   B. 22 L
   C. 32 L
   D. 68 L

32. What is 2 1/4 L + 1 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/2 L
   B. 4 L
   C. 3 3/4 L
   D. 4 1/4 L

33. An electronic balance shows 2.5 kg. Which mass is this? (1 mark)
   A. 25 kg
   B. 2 1/4 kg
   C. 2 3/4 kg
   D. 2 1/2 kg

34. What is 3 1/4 kg + 2 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 6 1/4 kg
   B. 5 3/4 kg
   C. 6 kg
   D. 5 1/2 kg

35. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 3 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 12. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 4:00
   B. 12:15
   C. 3:12
   D. 3:00

36. What is 6 h − 2 h 15 min? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 35 min
   B. 3 h 55 min
   C. 3 h 45 min
   D. 4 h 45 min

37. A customer pays with Ksh 5,000 for goods that cost Ksh 3,350. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 8,350
   B. Ksh 1,750
   C. Ksh 1,640
   D. Ksh 1,650

38. Kip faces South and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. West
   D. North

39. Kip faces West and makes a half turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North
   C. East
   D. South

40. What is a plane figure? (1 mark)
   A. A curved line only
   B. A solid object
   C. A kind of aeroplane
   D. A flat shape

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write 7,206 in expanded form. (2 marks)

42. Write 0.7, 0.07, 0.75 and 0.57 in order from the smallest to the largest. (3 marks)

43. A bus carried 5,684 passengers on Saturday and 3,749 on Sunday. Find the total number of passengers and check your answer by adding in the opposite order. (4 marks)

44. Explain why a table is better than raw data for answering questions. (3 marks)

45. A shop sells 3 packets of milk of 1/2 L each and 2 packets of 1 L each. How many litres of milk is that altogether? (3 marks)

46. A dial scale has big marks for each kilogram and three small marks between them. What mass does the first small mark after 3 kg show? Explain. (3 marks)

47. A signboard has four straight sides. Two sides are 50 cm and two are 30 cm. All four corners are square. Name the shape and give a reason. (3 marks)

48. Write an expression for each: (a) 6 less than k, (b) three times a number b, (c) the cost of 5 pens at p shillings each. (3 marks)

49. Rectangle P has 5 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area and by how much? (4 marks)

50. Write 4 3/8 as an improper fraction. (3 marks)

51. Change 250 cm to metres and centimetres, and then to metres using a decimal. (3 marks)

52. A ribbon is 1 metre long. Write 27 centimetres as a fraction of a metre and as a decimal. (3 marks)

53. Nanjala says an angle with longer arms is always bigger. Is she right? Explain. (3 marks)

54. Kip faces west and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? Explain. (3 marks)

55. A store stacks boxes 6 in a row, 3 rows deep and 2 layers high. How many boxes are in the stack? Give one safety rule for stacking. (4 marks)

56. Subtract 2 hours 35 minutes from 5 hours 20 minutes. (3 marks)

57. Write 5x + 3y − 2x + y in its simplest form. (3 marks)

58. Add 2 hours 45 minutes and 1 hour 30 minutes. (3 marks)

59. The mass of a basket full of mangoes is 8 kg and the basket alone is 1 1/2 kg. Find the mass of the mangoes alone. (2 marks)

60. A cuboid has a volume of 60 blocks. One layer has 12 blocks. How many layers does it have? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 6
   18 ÷ 6 = 3 with nothing left over, so 6 is a factor of 18. The others leave a remainder.

2. A — 4
   IV stands for 4.

3. C — 50
   Look at the ones digit 7. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 47 rounds to 50.

4. A — 30
   The rule is add 5. 25 + 5 = 30.

5. B — five hundred and eighty-three
   583 = five hundred and eighty-three. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

6. D — 9,000
   5,382 rounds to 5,380 and 3,617 rounds to 3,620. 5,380 + 3,620 = 9,000.

7. C — 8,833
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 6,478 + 2,355 = 8,833.

8. C — add 300
   Each number is 300 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 300.

9. C — Altogether
   Altogether means put the amounts together, so we add.

10. B — 400
   25 × 6 = 150 and 25 × 10 = 250. 150 + 250 = 400.

11. C — 1,200
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 12 × 100 = 1,200.

12. C — 336 eggs
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 336 eggs.

13. C — 23 remainder 3
   4 × 23 = 92 and 95 − 92 = 3. So 95 ÷ 4 = 23 remainder 3. Check: 23 × 4 + 3 = 95.

14. B — 8
   29 ÷ 4 = 7 remainder 1. The 1 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 8 trays are needed.

15. C — 3/8
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 3/8 is less than one whole.

16. B — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 3/5 it says that 3 parts are taken.

17. B — 5
   50 ÷ 10 = 5 and 5 × 1 = 5. So 1/10 of 50 is 5.

18. B — 5/12
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 5/12 is less than one whole.

19. D — 12
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

20. A — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 13.42 the digit 2 is in the hundredths place.

21. A — 37/100
   The last digit of 0.37 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.37 = 37/100.

22. D — a and b are different things, so the terms cannot be joined
   a and b stand for different kinds of things, so 2a and 3b are not like terms. The expression stays as 2a + 3b.

23. D — 905 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 9 × 100 = 900, and 900 + 5 = 905. So the answer is 905 cm.

24. B — 3 m 65 cm
   615 − 250 = 365 cm = 3 m 65 cm.

25. B — Square centimetres
   Area is measured in square units, such as square centimetres (cm²).

26. C — 9
   Rows × columns = 36, so columns = 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

27. C — 12
   Rows × columns = 60, so columns = 60 ÷ 5 = 12.

28. A — 64 square units
   Area = 8 × 8 = 64 square units.

29. B — Its length, width and height are equal
   A cube has 6 equal square faces, so its length, width and height are the same.

30. B — Cuboid B
   A = 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 blocks. B = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

31. C — 32 L
   50 − 18 = 32 L.

32. C — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 2 1/4 L + 1 1/2 L = 3 3/4 L.

33. D — 2 1/2 kg
   0.5 is half, so 2.5 kg is 2 1/2 kg.

34. B — 5 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 1/4 kg + 2 1/2 kg = 5 3/4 kg.

35. D — 3:00
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 12 shows 12 × 5 = 0 minutes, so the time is 3:00.

36. C — 3 h 45 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 3 h 45 min.

37. D — Ksh 1,650
   Change = amount paid − cost = 5,000 − 3,350 = Ksh 1,650.

38. A — East
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. South followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives East.

39. C — East
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. West followed by a half turn gives East.

40. D — A flat shape
   A plane figure is a flat shape with length and width but no thickness.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: 7,000 + 200 + 6
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7,000 and 200; 1 mark for 6 ones with no tens.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.07, 0.57, 0.7, 0.75
   Working / marking points: Write with two decimal places: 0.70, 0.07, 0.75, 0.57. 1 mark for 0.07 first, 2 marks for the rest in order.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: 9,433 passengers. Check: 3,749 + 5,684 = 9,433.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct working with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with unit, 1 mark for the check.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table puts the data in order under headings, is neat and easy to read, and shows totals. Raw data is untidy and easy to misread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point up to 3.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 L (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 L (1 mark); total 3 1/2 L (1 mark).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/4 kg. The three small marks divide each kilogram into four equal parts of 1/4 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 1/4 kg, 1 mark for four equal parts, 1 mark for 1/4 kg each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle, because opposite sides are equal but not all sides are equal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the name, 1 mark for opposite sides equal, 1 mark for not all sides equal.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) k − 6 (b) 3b (c) 5p
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct expression.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Q is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: P = 35 (1 mark); Q = 36 (1 mark); Q is bigger (1 mark); difference 1 (1 mark).

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: 35/8
   Working / marking points: 4 × 8 = 32 (1 mark); 32 + 3 = 35 (1 mark); denominator stays 8 (1 mark).

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 50 cm and 2.5 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by 100, 1 mark for 2 m 50 cm, 1 mark for 2.5 m.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: 27/100 m = 0.27 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying 1 m = 100 cm, 1 mark for 27/100, 1 mark for 0.27.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: No. The size of an angle depends on how far apart the arms are, not on how long they are.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no, 1 mark for the opening between the arms, 1 mark for length not mattering.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: Going clockwise the order is N, E, S, W and back to N (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Answer north (1 mark).

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: 36 boxes. Put heavy boxes at the bottom (or do not stack too high).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 6 × 3 = 18, 1 mark for 18 × 2, 1 mark for 36, 1 mark for a sensible safety rule.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: Change 5 h 20 min to 4 h 80 min (1 mark); 80 − 35 = 45 min (1 mark); 4 − 2 = 2 h, so 2 h 45 min (1 mark).

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3x + 4y
   Working / marking points: x terms: 5x − 2x = 3x (1 mark). y terms: 3y + y = 4y (1 mark). Answer 3x + 4y (1 mark).

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 hours 15 minutes
   Working / marking points: 45 + 30 = 75 min and 2 + 1 = 3 h (1 mark); 75 min = 1 h 15 min (1 mark); total 4 h 15 min (1 mark).

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 8 − 1 1/2 = 6 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5 layers
   Working / marking points: 60 ÷ 12 = 5. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.
